requirements.quote:
Implementations need to be able to parse and ignore unknown values
   unless the definition of the field states otherwise.
requirements.condition: an implementation receives an unknown enumerated value and the field definition does not specify different handling
requirements.required_behavior: parse the unknown value according to the enumerated field's wire width
requirements.forbidden_behavior: fail solely because the enumerated value is unknown
requirements.why_checkable: A field can be populated with an unassigned in-width value and tested for successful parsing.

requirements.quote:
Implementations need to be able to parse and ignore unknown values
   unless the definition of the field states otherwise.
requirements.condition: an implementation receives an unknown enumerated value and the field definition does not specify different handling
requirements.required_behavior: ignore the unknown value after parsing it
requirements.forbidden_behavior: assign defined-value semantics to the unknown value
requirements.why_checkable: Processing after a successfully parsed unknown enum can be observed for side effects or rejection.

requirements.quote:
An enumerated occupies as much space in the byte stream as would its
   maximal defined ordinal value.
requirements.condition: an enumerated type is encoded or decoded
requirements.required_behavior: use the wire width required by the type's maximal defined ordinal value
requirements.forbidden_behavior: vary the enum width by the selected element or use a width too small for the maximal ordinal
requirements.why_checkable: The enum definition fixes a deterministic byte width for every value.

requirements.quote:
One may optionally specify a value without its associated tag to
   force the width definition without defining a superfluous element.
requirements.condition: an enum definition contains an untagged numerical value
requirements.required_behavior: include that value when determining the enum's wire width
requirements.forbidden_behavior: ignore the untagged value when determining the width
requirements.why_checkable: The resulting enum width can be compared with the width required by the untagged value.

requirements.quote:
In the following example, Taste will consume two bytes in the data
   stream but can only assume the values 1, 2, or 4 in the current
   version of the protocol.

      enum { sweet(1), sour(2), bitter(4), (32000) } Taste;
requirements.condition: an enum definition contains an untagged value used only to force its width
requirements.required_behavior: treat only tagged values or tagged ranges as currently defined enum values
requirements.forbidden_behavior: treat the untagged width-forcing value as a defined enum element
requirements.why_checkable: The parser's known-value set can be tested independently from the width forced by the anonymous value.

requirements.quote:
The
   numerical value can describe a range over which the same name
   applies.  The value includes the minimum and maximum inclusive values
   in that range, separated by two period characters.
requirements.condition: an enumerated element is declared with a minimum..maximum range
requirements.required_behavior: apply that element name to every numerical value from the minimum through the maximum inclusive
requirements.forbidden_behavior: exclude either endpoint from the declared range
requirements.why_checkable: Tests at both endpoints and adjacent values can verify inclusive range handling.
